bib.title: Benchmarking Large Language Models for News Summarization

read.skipped: none; references skimmed; no appendix exists

question: What drives LLM zero-shot news summarization quality, and are LLM summaries comparable to those of human writers once reference quality is controlled?
hypothesis: Instruction tuning rather than model scale explains zero-shot summarization; poor references depress metric correlation and few-shot/fine-tuning results.
contributions: Identify instruction tuning, not scale, as key to LLM summarization
Show XSUM references are judged worse than best LLM summaries
Collect freelance-writer summaries and show best LLM is rated comparable; release them and evaluation data

method.summary: Human (MTurk) evaluation of 10 LLMs, 2 fine-tuned models and existing references on 100 CNN/DM and 100 XSUM articles; then freelance writer summaries on 50+50 articles and a 6-annotator pairwise comparison against Instruct Davinci; metric correlations at system level.

datasets.name: CNN/DM
datasets.size: 100 validation articles (human eval); 50 articles re-annotated by freelancers
datasets.preprocessing: five 5-shot demos sampled from train, 50-150 GPT-2 tokens

datasets.name: XSUM
datasets.size: 100 validation articles (human eval); 50 articles re-annotated by freelancers
datasets.preprocessing: demos hand-picked from train; freelancers got full articles, not preprocessed version

other.note: generated empty outputs, omitted from human evaluation

inference.samples: inferred: one summary per article per model setting; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot and five-shot (five train examples); CNN/DM 'summarize in three sentences', XSUM 'one sentence'; zero-shot only for 3 GPT-3 and 3 instruct GPT-3 models; Section 4 prompt asks 25 words to get ~50 word summaries

other.api_naming_note: instruction-tuning details of instruct GPT-3 inferred from API names

metrics.name: Faithfulness
metrics.definition: binary rating per Fabbri et al. 2020 guidelines, mean of 3 annotators

metrics.name: Kendall tau (system-level)
metrics.definition: rank correlation of metric vs human score over systems; Rouge-L, METEOR, BertScore, BARTScore, BLEURT

metrics.name: Coverage / density
metrics.definition: Grusky et al. 2018: % summary words in article / average length of copied spans

eval.protocol: MTurk 3 annotators per summary, $15/hr; significance tests marked in Table 2 (test not named); Section 4: 6 Upwork writers, $4/article, 3 writers per article, 6 annotators judging the same 100 pairs; fluency omitted

availability.data: freelance summaries and evaluation data released at same URL
